    Pointwise-thin finite-dimensional modules #

    For modules on a basic finite or locally bounded linear category, multiplicity-freeness is expressed by having coefficient-field dimension at most one at every object. This is the form supplied by the universal-cover equality calculation.

    source
    def MagnitudeConjecture.CoveringHom.IsPointwiseThin {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] (M : CategoryTheory.Functor C (ModuleCat k)) :
    Prop

    A linear module is pointwise thin when every value has dimension at most one over the coefficient field.

      IsPointwiseThin M ↔ ∀ (X : C), ¬CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (M.obj X) → Module.finrank k ↑(M.obj X) = 1

      For a pointwise finite module, pointwise thinness is equivalently the statement that every nonzero value has dimension one.
